discussion_comments.comment_body: Addressed in 7a5dc22a. Switched from `execSync` with template-literal interpolation to `execFileSync` with an argument array (no shell). Added a strict `SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/` check enforced before any FS or zip call — invalid slugs fail the run before being passed to any subprocess.

Addressed in d3bf855c. New isSafeCanonicalId() basename guard rejects anything that doesn't match `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$` or that contains `..`. Rejected entries increment a new `result.skippedInvalidId` counter so the dry-run/summary surfaces them. The manifest is trusted today, but the defensive check prevents a malformed entry from writing outside commands_target_dir.

**Resolved in fb57c81. This was a real, reproducible attack vector — thanks for catching it.**

I confirmed the exploit on the previous commit before fixing:

```
$ node -e "
  const { parseSetEntries } = require('./tools/installer/set-overrides');
  console.log('Before:', ({}).polluted);
  parseSetEntries(['__proto__.polluted=1']);
  console.log('After:', ({}).polluted);
"
Before: undefined
After: 1               # ← Object.prototype polluted
```

Applied both your suggested defenses:

1. `parseSetEntry` now rejects `__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` as either the module or the key segment with a clear error.
2. `parseSetEntries` builds the outer and inner maps with `Object.create(null)` for defense-in-depth — even if a future caller bypasses the parser, lookups can't traverse `Object.prototype`.

Verified post-fix: the same exploit string now exits 1 with `'__proto__', 'prototype', and 'constructor' are reserved...` and `({}).polluted` stays `undefined`. Test coverage added for both rejection paths.

Fixed — added `|| options.scope === "." || options.scope === ".."` to CLI validation. Also tightened `module.yaml` regex to require at least one alphanumeric character, so interactive prompts reject dot-segments at input time too.

**Fixed** in 11b891c0 — Added defense-in-depth validation in `resolveSkillName`: rejects canonicalIds containing path separators, `..`, or whitespace, falling back to path-derived name. Actual severity is LOW (data source is trusted version-controlled YAML), but the fix is cheap.

Thanks for the review. The validator intentionally does not trim `workflow-file` values.

The CLI's `parseCsvLine()` in `installer.js` accumulates field characters verbatim — no `.trim()`. LLM agents consuming the CSV at runtime also receive the raw value. If whitespace were introduced into a `workflow-file` cell, it would be a real data bug that both runtime consumers and the validator should flag.

Adding `.trim()` to the validator would make validation more lenient than the code that actually consumes the data. Defensive coding in a validator that broadens acceptable input beyond what the consuming code handles breaks the purpose of the validator — it would silently bless data that fails at runtime.

If/when all CSV consumers are proven to trim, the validator will match. Until then, strictness here is correct.
